findings.issue_text: Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11` indexes `execute(...)[0]['id']` for the `embed_category` site setting without a nil guard, raising NoMethodError and hard-failing the migration/deploy when the query returns zero rows
Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15` uses the same unguarded `[0]['value']` on the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup, crashing the migration if that row is absent

Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` inserts hosts verbatim, bypassing the model's `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths, so migrated rows like `http://discourse.org` never match `record_for_host`'s `URI#host` comparison and embedding silently breaks on upgraded sites

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6` calls `self.host.sub!(...)` in `before_validation`, raising NoMethodError (500) when `host` is nil instead of returning a validation error; reachable from `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create`

`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:15-16` uses `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`, so an unknown id yields nil and `host.destroy` raises NoMethodError (500) instead of 404; the same nil flows into `save_host` from `#update` at lines 10-11

Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` interpolates the host value directly into the INSERT string (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), allowing SQL breakage/injection from apostrophes or metacharacters in the old setting; should use `quote(h)` or bound parameters

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17` uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without downcasing the bind value, so referers with uppercase (e.g. `http://EvilTrout.com`) are rejected and uppercase rows never match

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197-201` unconditionally runs `delete obj[k]` in the new plural branch and `obj[k].map(...)` yields `undefined` entries when referenced records aren't side-loaded, losing the raw ids (the singular branch preserves the key); `hydrated || []` is dead code since `map` always returns an array

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197` calls `obj[k].map` without a type check, throwing if the server sends `"foo_ids": null` or a non-array, unlike the old code which tolerated any value

`app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` without `include: true`, so host objects are never side-loaded into the root and `_hydrateEmbedded` renders empty/undefined rows in the admin table

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb` lacks a uniqueness validation and unique index on `host`, and `record_for_host` uses `.first` without an `order`, so duplicate host rows make the category for new embedded topics nondeterministic

Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-7` creates no index on `host` (and `where("lower(host) = ?")` couldn't use a plain index), making `ensure_embeddable` do a sequential scan on every public `/embed/comments` request; needs a functional index on `lower(host)`

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46` omits `.catch(popupAjaxError)` on `destroyRecord().then(...)`, so a failed delete is swallowed with no error shown and the row silently remains

`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert class ancestry, with no coverage of create/update/destroy behavior, the uncategorized-category fallback, or the admin-only constraint on the new write endpoints

`test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6:110` calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but the pretender's `/fruits/:id` handler ignores the id and always returns `fruits[0]`, so the assertions describe apple rather than banana and the test passes while asserting the wrong record

`spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1401` test `"is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer exercises host behavior (the condition was removed from `expandable_first_post?`) and only passes because `embed_truncate` defaults to false; it should be deleted or renamed

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22` uses `type.replace('_', '-')`, replacing only the first underscore, so admin models with two or more underscores won't match `ADMIN_MODELS`; should use `replace(/_/g, '-')`

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,17` validation regex permits a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) that `before_validation` doesn't strip, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host` which excludes the port, so a host saved as `example.com:8080` can never match
Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3` uses `create_table ..., force: true`, silently dropping a pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table (e.g. from a plugin) and its data

Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb` puts `execute` calls including a destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings` inside `change`, so rollback raises `IrreversibleMigration` and the old settings are unrecoverable

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:6` `saveChanges` issues `update({})` against `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, which ignores params and just re-renders; the action isn't wired to anything in `embedding.hbs`, making it dead code implying a nonexistent save step

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` and `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have swapped contents — the category fabricators live in the embeddable-host file and vice versa — making both undiscoverable by filename

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197-201` unconditionally runs `delete obj[k]` in the new plural branch and `obj[k].map(...)` yields `undefined` entries when referenced records aren't side-loaded, losing the raw ids (the singular branch preserves the key); `hydrated || []` is dead code since `map` always returns an array

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` the new plural-handling branch (`/_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]` truthy) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and then **always** `delete obj[k]`. Unlike the singular branch (which only deletes the `*_id` key when a `hydrated` record is found), this will remove the raw `*_ids` array even when `_lookupSubType` returns null/undefined for some or all ids (e.g., when referenced records are not side-loaded), leaving `obj[pluralizedSubType]` containing undefined entries and losing the original ids for later use. Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively dead since `Array#map` always returns an array (it won’t be falsy).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:197` calls `obj[k].map` without a type check, throwing if the server sends `"foo_ids": null` or a non-array, unlike the old code which tolerated any value

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` the `_hydrateEmbedded` logic was expanded to match keys ending in `_ids` and, when matched (`m[2]` truthy), it unconditionally does `obj[k].map(function(id) { ... })`. There is no guard that `obj[k]` is actually an Array, so a payload like `{ foo_ids: null }` (or any non-array) will throw `TypeError: Cannot read property 'map' of null` at runtime. The prior code path for `_id` did not call `.map` and would tolerate `nil`/unexpected values via `_lookupSubType`. This is a concrete behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` without `include: true`, so host objects are never side-loaded into the root and `_hydrateEmbedded` renders empty/undefined rows in the admin table

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb` lacks a uniqueness validation and unique index on `host`, and `record_for_host` uses `.first` without an `order`, so duplicate host rows make the category for new embedded topics nondeterministic

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an `embeddable_hosts` table (`db/migrate/...create_embeddable_hosts.rb`) with no unique index on `host`, and the model `EmbeddableHost` validates only format (no `validates :host, uniqueness: ...`). The admin controller `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` also does not check for existing hosts before saving, so duplicate rows are allowed. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` without an explicit `order`, so if duplicates exist, which row is returned (and thus which `category_id` is used in `TopicEmbed.import` via `eh.try(:category_id)`) is not deterministic at the SQL level. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3-7` creates no index on `host` (and `where("lower(host) = ?")` couldn't use a plain index), making `ensure_embeddable` do a sequential scan on every public `/embed/comments` request; needs a functional index on `lower(host)`

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts(host, category_id, ...)` with no index on `host`. The runtime authorization path for embeds (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` -> `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` -> `record_for_host`) performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` for every embed request. Without an index, this lookup will require a sequential scan as the table grows, and a normal index on `host` would not be used for the `lower(host)` predicate in Postgres (you’d need a functional index on `lower(host)` or normalize `host` to lowercase on write and index the column). This is a concrete performance defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46` omits `.catch(popupAjaxError)` on `destroyRecord().then(...)`, so a failed delete is swallowed with no error shown and the row silently remains

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but does not attach a `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save()`, which does). If the DELETE request fails, the rejection is not handled here, so the user will not see the standard popup error, and `deleteHost` will not be sent—leaving the row in place with no explicit feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert class ancestry, with no coverage of create/update/destroy behavior, the uncategorized-category fallback, or the admin-only constraint on the new write endpoints

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, both `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` contain only a single example asserting the controller inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. They do not exercise any of the newly added behaviors/endpoints (`create/update/destroy` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, `show/update` in `Admin::EmbeddingController`), nor do they verify the `uncategorized_category_id` fallback in `save_host`, nor any authorization behavior around the new write routes. This lack of meaningful test coverage is directly observable in the added spec files.

adjudication.rationale: The proposed finding references `test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` and a Pretender handler for `/fruits/:id`, but this diff does not include that test file, any Pretender setup, or any code related to `fruit`/`fruits`. Since the alleged issue is not present or modified in the provided diff, it is not a verifiable problem introduced or exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1401` test `"is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer exercises host behavior (the condition was removed from `expandable_first_post?`) and only passes because `embed_truncate` defaults to false; it should be deleted or renamed

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` to remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard (it now only checks `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). Therefore, any spec asserting the method is false specifically because “embeddable_host(s) is blank” would no longer be exercising that condition; the result would instead be driven by `embed_truncate` (which defaults to false per `site_settings.yml`). That makes such a test misleading/obsolete and it should be removed or renamed/rewritten to reflect the new logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22` uses `type.replace('_', '-')`, replacing only the first underscore, so admin models with two or more underscores won't match `ADMIN_MODELS`; should use `replace(/_/g, '-')`

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `basePath(store, type)` now checks `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-')) !== -1`. While it’s true that `String#replace('_','-')` only replaces the first underscore, every admin model added/used here (`embeddable_host`, `site_customization`, `plugin`) has at most one underscore (or none), so the current code will match `ADMIN_MODELS` correctly for all cases shown/implicated by this change. The finding only becomes an issue if an admin model type with multiple underscores is introduced into `ADMIN_MODELS`, which is not present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2,17` validation regex permits a port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) that `before_validation` doesn't strip, but `record_for_host` compares against `URI#host` which excludes the port, so a host saved as `example.com:8080` can never match

adjudication.rationale: Yes. `EmbeddableHost` allows a port in the `host` attribute via the validation regex `(:[0-9]{1,5})?`, and the `before_validation` hook strips scheme and path but does not strip a `:port`. Meanwhile `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(...)` and uses `uri.host` (which excludes the port) to query `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. Therefore, if an admin saves `example.com:8080`, it will be stored with the port, but lookups for `http://example.com:8080/...` will search for `example.com` and never match the stored `example.com:8080`, making such entries ineffective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3` uses `create_table ..., force: true`, silently dropping a pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table (e.g. from a plugin) and its data

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will DROP the table if it already exists before recreating it, which can silently destroy any existing `embeddable_hosts` data (regardless of why the table exists). This destructive behavior is explicitly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration `create_embeddable_hosts.rb` puts `execute` calls including a destructive `DELETE FROM site_settings` inside `change`, so rollback raises `IrreversibleMigration` and the old settings are unrecoverable

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration is defined with `def change` but performs multiple raw `execute` SQL statements (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE), including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot automatically reverse arbitrary `execute` calls inside `change`, so `rake db:rollback` will raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration` (unless wrapped in a `reversible` block or split into `up`/`down`). Separately, the DELETE permanently removes the old settings data, so even if the migration were made reversible later, the original settings values are not preserved by this migration.
